title: "Robotics and Control"
description: "Research in energy-based control, dynamic manipulation, locomotion, and coordinated robotic systems."

::: {.research-page}

::: {.research-lead}
How can robots use their natural dynamics to move and manipulate objects?
:::

Robots must work within physical constraints: limited actuation, changing contact, and the motion of the objects around them. Our research uses nonlinear control, geometric mechanics, and optimization to study these systems and design feedback for them.

## Energy shaping and underactuated systems

An underactuated robot has fewer independent control inputs than degrees of freedom. This makes the relationship between its natural motion and its control inputs especially important.

Our work studies **passivity-based control**, which approaches feedback design through the system's energy and its exchange with the environment. We also investigate data-driven methods for solving the equations that arise in energy-shaping controller design.

::: {.research-paper}

**Representative work**

[Data-Driven Passivity-Based Control of Underactuated Mechanical Systems via Interconnection and Damping Assignment](https://doi.org/10.1080/00207179.2022.2051750) uses neural approximations to formulate the controller-design equations as an optimization problem.

[Publication and Scholar search](../publications.qmd#ref-satici2022ijc) · [Related learning research](robust_machine_learning.qmd#learning-to-design-controllers)

:::

## Dynamic manipulation

Manipulation includes tasks in which an object is not continuously held in a rigid grasp. Tossing, catching, and batting require reasoning about the motion of both the robot and the object.

Our work includes a coordinate-free treatment of robotic pizza tossing and catching, as well as trajectory planning for robotic batting. These studies connect geometric descriptions of motion with task-specific control problems.

- [A coordinate-free framework for robotic pizza tossing and catching](../publications.qmd#ref-satici2016coordinate) — ICRA, 2016. [Author's paper](https://www.fabioruggiero.name/web/files/Papers/C19.pdf).
- [An Optimal Trajectory Planner for a Robotic Batting Task: The Table Tennis Example](../publications.qmd#ref-serra2016optimal) — ICINCO, 2016.

## Locomotion and coordinated motion

We study motion across systems ranging from walking models to groups of mobile robots. Representative topics include energy-efficient stabilization of a rimless wheel with a torso, optimal control of a biped, and formation control with connectivity and collision constraints.

- [Energetically-optimal discrete and continuous stabilization of the rimless wheel with torso](../publications.qmd#ref-sirichotiyakul2019energetically).
- [Optimal Control of a 5-Link Biped Using Quadratic Polynomial Model of Two-Point Boundary Value Problem](../publications.qmd#ref-hernandez2021optimal).
- [Collision-Free Formation Control with Decentralized Connectivity Preservation for Nonholonomic-Wheeled Mobile Robots](../publications.qmd#ref-Poonawala14a).
